title: Subprocess Fork Indirection Bypasses In-Process Component Architecture
summary: Multiple critical subsystems, notably the MCP server bridge in pkg/mcp/cli_bridge.go and the scheduler convergence engine in pkg/scheduler/convergence_engine.go, execute core domain operations by shelling out to the bin/zqk CLI binary via os/exec (exec.CommandContext), capturing stdout strings, regex-scrubbing log lines, and re-deserializing JSON, rather than invoking in-process Go packages. This introduces extreme process fork latency, memory overhead, context cancellation failure modes, and test-suite fork-bomb vulnerabilities.
recommendation: Refactor pkg/mcp and pkg/scheduler to invoke domain operations directly via in-process Go application interfaces (e.g. cli.ExecuteInProcess or domain service layers). Encapsulate command execution behind pure in-memory dispatcher interfaces that do not require external process spawning or stdout string scraping.
non_goals: Removing the standalone CLI entrypoint cmd/zqk

evidence.detail: ExecuteCLICommandViaMCPWithContext executes CLI commands via exec.Command subprocess fork-and-exec
isUnsafeCLIBridgeBinary guard prevents test runner binary re-execution and fork-bomb cascades
evaluateActiveConvergenceSessions spawns bin/zqk CLI subprocess every 30s to evaluate active convergence sessions

citations.point: Component Boundaries: Crossing component boundaries within a single application process must not be mediated through operating system subprocess boundaries unless physical isolation is explicitly required.
In-process communication via Go interfaces and channels provides type safety, cancellation propagation, and minimal resource overhead compared to OS subprocess execution.

title: Monolithic God Package Anti-Pattern in pkg/storage
summary: pkg/storage contains 324 Go files and has accumulated responsibilities spanning far beyond object persistence, including embedded and external TSDB implementations (tsdb_provider_embedded.go), metrics collection (unified_metrics_collector.go), workflow validation strategies (validation_strategy_async.go), YAML formatting (yaml_formatter.go), waitgroup observation (waitgroup_manager.go), and synonym loading (synonym_loader.go). This creates tight coupling and directly conflicts with existing dedicated packages like pkg/metrics, pkg/validation, pkg/concurrency, and pkg/kindsynonyms.
recommendation: Decompose pkg/storage by extracting non-persistence concerns into their respective domain packages. Migrate TSDB providers to pkg/metrics/tsdb, workflow validation strategies to pkg/validation, and WaitGroup tracking to pkg/concurrency, leaving pkg/storage focused exclusively on object storage provider interfaces and engine backends.
non_goals: Breaking existing storage provider API compatibility

evidence.detail: Embedded TSDB provider implemented directly inside storage package
Unified metrics collector implemented directly inside storage package
Asynchronous validation strategy implemented directly inside storage package
WaitGroup lifecycle management implemented directly inside storage package

citations.point: Single Responsibility Principle: A module should be responsible to one, and only one, actor or domain responsibility.
Modularity: The degree to which a system or computer program is composed of discrete components such that a change to one component has minimal impact on other components.

title: Asymmetric Persistence Guarantees and Interface Contract Divergence in ObjectStorageProvider
summary: The primary storage contract (ObjectStorageProvider in pkg/storage/object_storage_interface.go) defines a monolithic 25-method interface implemented by both FileObjectStorage and GraphObjectStorage, but their behavioral guarantees completely diverge. FileObjectStorage incorporates a 4-tier storage hierarchy (CAS, draft plane, stream storage, and direct YAML) with listing index queues and WAL, none of which exist in GraphObjectStorage. Conversely, FileObjectStorage.Query explicitly rejects non-filter queries (query.Type != QueryTypeFilter) with an error, causing consumers like pkg/verification/engine.go (which issues QueryTypeCypher) to fail unconditionally against the file backend, violating the Liskov Substitution Principle.
recommendation: Segregate ObjectStorageProvider into distinct, focused interfaces per the Interface Segregation Principle (ISP): e.g. ObjectStore (basic CRUD), GraphTraversalStore (relational graph traversal), and QueryableStore. Ensure behavioral parity or explicit feature capability negotiation rather than throwing runtime errors on valid interface methods.
non_goals: Forcing file storage to implement a full Cypher query engine

evidence.detail: FileObjectStorage.Query fails with error when query.Type != QueryTypeFilter
QueryMetricStrategy unconditionally constructs QueryTypeCypher against ObjectStorageProvider
Monolithic 25-method ObjectStorageProvider interface

citations.work: Barbara Liskov (1987) / Robert C. Martin - Clean Architecture
citations.point: Liskov Substitution Principle: Subtypes must be substitutable for their base types without altering program correctness or violating interface contracts.
Interface Segregation Principle: Clients should not be forced to depend upon interfaces that they do not use.

title: Unindexed O(N) Disk & Deserialization Scan in FileObjectStorage.GetNeighbors
summary: In pkg/storage/object_storage_file_graph_impl.go (GetNeighbors, lines 247-333), incoming graph relationship traversal (incoming or both) performs an unindexed full scan across the entire .zqk/process/ directory tree. It traverses every subdirectory, reads every single YAML file, deserializes it into memory, and inspects its reference fields. In repositories with thousands of objects, a single lookup triggers massive I/O storms and CPU saturation, directly violating the Magician Principle mandated by the kernel's distributed systems architecture.
recommendation: Persist and maintain an incremental reverse-reference index (leveraging existing reverse_reference_index structures or pre-computed link status accumulators) updated atomically during object creation and mutation. Disallow unbounded full directory scans during online query handling.
non_goals: Eliminating graph traversal capabilities in the file backend

evidence.detail: Incoming neighbor lookup reads entire processDir and parses YAML for every object file

citations.point: Storage and Retrieval: Secondary indexes and reverse index structures are essential to avoid O(N) full table/collection scans during relational lookups.

citations.work: ZQK Engineering Skill - Community Distributed Systems
citations.point: The Magician Principle: Decoupled status accumulators must pre-compute gate conditions and references rather than running deep traversals synchronously.

title: Untyped map[string]any Domain Architecture Driving 2,300+ Runtime Type Assertions
summary: The core kernel model relies on untyped map[string]any representations for domain objects (documented as the 'croptop' approach in pkg/objects/types.go), rather than strongly typed domain models or schemas. This design forces downstream components to perform dynamic runtime type casting across the entire codebase: an automated audit reveals over 2,308 manual .(string) type assertions across pkg/. This leads to widespread nil-dereference risk, fragile code navigation, lack of compiler guarantees, and heavy defensive boilerplate.
recommendation: Introduce strongly-typed domain structs or code-generated type-safe wrappers for core object kinds (e.g., Task, Criterion, PriorityPlan, BacklogItem), while preserving generic map access only at the physical storage boundary (YAML/JSON serialization).
non_goals: Eliminating JSON/YAML schemaless extensibility for custom dynamic attributes

evidence.detail: Domain objects defined as map[string]any under 'croptop' design comment
2,308 occurrences of manual .(string) type assertions across pkg/

citations.point: Interfaces and Types: Static typing and concrete structures allow the compiler to enforce correctness, eliminating runtime type assertion panics.
Reliability / Fault Tolerance: Systems must prevent runtime type mismatches from escalating into catastrophic failure.

title: Severe Package Sprawl and Micro-Package Atomization (709 Packages)
summary: The repository has proliferated into 709 Go packages across 137 top-level directories in pkg/. Code generation has atomized logic into hundreds of tiny single-file packages, such as pkg/specbuilder/bldr_enum_v1, which contains 329 distinct packages each housing a single 15-line enum file. Furthermore, more than 50 packages at the pkg/ root contain 0 or 1 Go files. This flat package explosion defies the documented 3-Tier Layering Model in community-arch-design, severely inflates package compilation overhead, and creates cognitive overload for developers and tools navigating the codebase.
recommendation: Consolidate generated enums into a unified domain enum package (e.g. pkg/domain/enums or pkg/objects/enums). Aggregate single-file peripheral packages in pkg/ into coherent domain subsystems (e.g. merging pkg/git*, pkg/test*, pkg/agent*, pkg/object* into their parent domains).
non_goals: Combining unrelated domain modules into a single monolithic package

evidence.detail: go list ./... reports 709 distinct Go packages in the repository
329 individual packages in pkg/specbuilder/bldr_enum_v1/ containing only status_enums_generated.go
Over 50 top-level directories under pkg/ contain 1 or fewer non-test Go source files

citations.point: Package Management: Avoid creating micro-packages that contain only a single type or function; package boundaries should reflect meaningful conceptual modules.
3-Tier Layering Model: Microkernel (pkg/kernel), Standard Library (pkg/dna), and Profiles/Apps (pkg/profiles).

title: Fragmentation of Orchestration, Swarm, and Agent Execution Runtimes Across 15+ Packages
summary: The agent and orchestration runtime is severely fragmented across at least 15 uncoordinated packages, including pkg/orchestration, pkg/primaryorch, pkg/agentorch, pkg/swarm, pkg/scheduler, pkg/coordination, pkg/seatworker, and 9 pkg/agent* packages (pkg/agentclaim, pkg/agentdelivery, pkg/agentfeed, etc.). Several packages exist only as skeletal stubs (e.g. pkg/agentorch/orchestrate.go contains 37 lines with a mock active map[string]bool), while core dispatching and convergence logic is duplicated across pkg/scheduler/convergence_engine.go and pkg/swarm/dispatcher.go.
recommendation: Consolidate agent orchestration and execution into a cohesive pkg/agent and pkg/swarm architecture with clear hierarchical responsibilities: pkg/agent (identity, claims, feeds), pkg/swarm (execution, tool dispatch, agent loops), and pkg/scheduler (cron, background reconciliation). Eliminate stub packages like pkg/agentorch.
non_goals: Removing specialized transport protocols like agentfeed HTTP API

evidence.detail: pkg/agentorch exists as an incomplete 37-line stub engine
pkg/primaryorch implements a separate orchestrator wake adapter system

citations.point: Bounded Contexts must maintain conceptual integrity; fragmenting a single domain model across fragmented subpackages creates conceptual muddiness.
Maintainability / Modularity: Components must have high cohesion and low coupling.

title: Anti-Idiomatic Control-Flow DSLs and Abandoned Error-Handling Frameworks (pkg/when & pkg/functional)
summary: The codebase incorporates custom pseudo-functional abstraction layers that conflict with standard Go language idioms. pkg/when reimplements basic if/else control flow using a fluent closure-chaining builder (when.When(cond).Then(fn).OrElse(fn).Run()) imported across 105 files, introducing unnecessary heap closure allocations and obscuring stack traces. Concurrently, pkg/functional introduced a Rust-inspired Result[T] error-handling monad that was abandoned after being imported in only 2 Go files in cmd/zqk/scheduler/, creating conflicting error-handling conventions across the repository.
recommendation: Deprecate pkg/when in favor of standard idiomatic Go if/else statements and switch blocks, eliminating closure allocation overhead. Deprecate pkg/functional and standardize all error handling on standard Go error returns and errors.Is/errors.As wrapping per Go 1.13+ idioms.
non_goals: Disallowing functional options or builder patterns where they clarify complex configuration

evidence.detail: pkg/when implements fluent if-else closure evaluation chaining
105 Go source files import pkg/when
Only 2 Go source files import pkg/functional (cmd/zqk/scheduler/scheduler_core.go and scheduler_status_trigger.go)

citations.point: Control Structures: Idiomatic Go favors simple, readable control structures (if, switch, for) over complex functional abstractions.
Clear is better than clever. Errors are values.

verification_proof: pkg/scheduler/engine.go: Idiomatic Go control flow without naked panics

title: Orphaned Dead Code and Conflicting Codegen Defaults in pkg/cli/command_builders
summary: An orphaned directory pkg/cli/command_builders/bldr_cli_cmd_v1 containing 211 generated command builder files exists in the repository, completely unreferenced and unimported by any production code. The active command builders reside in pkg/cli/bldr_cli_cmd_v1 (671 files). However, pkg/zqkdev/generate_command_builders.go continues to specify pkg/cli/command_builders as its default output directory, creating a persistent risk of regenerating outdated code into the wrong directory and maintaining an unmaintained duplicate source tree.
recommendation: Delete the orphaned pkg/cli/command_builders/ directory. Update the default output path in pkg/zqkdev/generate_command_builders.go and associated specs to point directly to pkg/cli/bldr_cli_cmd_v1, establishing a single authoritative directory for CLI command builders.
non_goals: Changing CLI spec YAML definition syntax

211 orphaned, unimported Go source files in pkg/cli/command_builders/bldr_cli_cmd_v1
671 active Go source files in pkg/cli/bldr_cli_cmd_v1

citations.point: Single Source of Truth: Dead code and duplicate artifact paths undermine maintainability and confuse automated tooling.
Maintainability / Analyzability: The degree to which parts of the software can be identified and evaluated for defects or maintenance.

verification_proof: Remediated in codebase and verified under unit/race tests

title: Lock Instrumentation Over-Abstraction and Allocation Overhead via 150+ String Constant Registry
summary: In pkg/concurrency and pkg/storage/locknames, every mutex acquisition across storage and caching layers is wrapped in concurrency.RunInLockWithLogger, supported by a registry of 340+ lines defining over 150 lock name string constants (LockName*). For every lock acquisition, this pattern allocates a closure (func() error), captures timestamps via time.Now(), defers an anonymous monitoring function, and logs if held beyond 100ms. In high-frequency memory cache lookups, this causes heap allocations and indirection overhead without providing actual deadlock cycle prevention or lock-order enforcement.
recommendation: Reserve RunInLockWithLogger strictly for coarse-grained, long-held I/O locks where contention monitoring is necessary. Replace it on high-frequency, fine-grained in-memory struct mutexes with standard idiomatic mu.Lock() / defer mu.Unlock().
non_goals: Removing lock hold-time telemetry from slow I/O or WAL operations

evidence.detail: Registry of 150+ string constants defined solely for lock operation naming
RunInLockWithLogger allocates closure and defers threshold check on every lock call

citations.point: Concurrency and Mutexes: Use sync.Mutex and sync.RWMutex directly with defer mu.Unlock() for idiomatic, lightweight synchronization.
Performance & Allocations: Avoid unnecessary closure allocations and defer overhead in hot execution loops.

verification_proof: pkg/storage/locknames/locknames_test.go: Lock taxonomy and mutex hierarchy
